title: Promote rule rejects deployed content when the release commit moves main
description:
The computer image promote rule requires the latest deploy-controlplane-<env> and deploy-thinturn-<env> runs to have succeeded for the exact commit being promoted. The release job pushes a chore(release) commit to main after each feature merge, so main moves between the deploys and the promote. The build workflow skips release commits ([skip ci]), so the image is built only for the previous commit.

Feature: Promote computer image
  Scenario: Release commit follows a deployed feature commit
    Given a feature commit was deployed and then a chore(release) commit touching only CHANGELOG.md and package files landed on main
    When promote-computer-image is run for the release commit or the deployed commit
    Then the promote accepts it because the content matches the deployed commit
  Scenario: Real content change
    Given a descendant commit changes files other than CHANGELOG.md and package*.json
    When promote-computer-image is run for it
    Then the promote is refused until that content is deployed

Approach options: compare the tree of the promoted commit with the deployed commits, or accept a descendant whose diff is only CHANGELOG.md and package*.json.
right_now_summary: Promote rejects release commits because main moves after deployment, even when only metadata files changed.
